title: Sub-10 K Monochromated Electron Energy-loss Spectroscopy for Two-dimensional Semiconductor van der Waals Heterostructures
content: Van der Waals heterostructures fabricated with semiconducting transition metal dichalcogenides (TMDs) with spin-valley coupling of carriers in different layers have attracted considerable attention because of their interesting properties that can be used for spin/valleytronic applications [1,2]. The lattice mismatch and/or twist angle between heterobilayers lead to variations in the local atomic registry in the form of a moiré periodicity, which cannot be resolved by conventional optical methods with limited spatial resolution [1]. As such, correlation of structural variations directly to the local excitonic behaviour is often lacking. An ideal technique to overcome this is aberration-corrected scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-STEM) capable of resolving the sub-nanometer scale periodicities combined with high energy resolution for measuring the excitonic resonances using electron energy-loss spectroscopy (EELS) [3]. In addition, due to thermal broadening and dielectric disorder-induced broadening of the linewidths and electron beam damage of atomically thin layers, cryogenic cooling and encapsulation of the specimen encapsulation with hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) are necessary to resolve fine energy separation of the excitonic resonances.
